pool.text: Juan Rodriguez Cabrillo claimed the area for Spain, laying the settlement basis.
The Presidio and Mission San Diego de Alcalá formed the first European settlement.
San Diego became part of the newly declared Mexican Empire.
California was admitted to the United States as the thirty first state.
San Diego remained a backwater town until a railroad connection arrived.
The city established a new city charter which was adopted.
San Diego hosted the California Pacific International Exposition as a World's Fair.
San Diego acquired its first television station, KFMB, which began broadcasting on May sixteenth.
The FCC began licensing UHF channels to allow cities to acquire more stations.
The city decided to replace the lights with more efficient sodium vapor lamps.
The city marked its deadliest year by registering 179 homicides within city limits.
San Diego was the site of the Cedar Fire wildfire.
The libraries have had reduced operating hours due to the city's financial problems.
Petco Park officially opened in downtown San Diego.
San Diego achieved the sixth lowest crime rate of any U.S. city.
Two city council members were convicted of extortion, wire fraud, and conspiracy charges.
Representative Cunningham was sentenced to a long prison sentence.
The city increased its financial spending on local libraries by two million dollars.
California wildfires destroyed areas particularly within Rancho Bernardo.
The Port of San Diego handled short tons of total trade.
